```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 06_probability_pair_of_dice
title: >
  Counting with two dice
questions:
  - id: sum_nine
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Using the table of 36 outcomes, what is the probability of rolling a sum
      of 9 with two fair dice?
    hint: >
      Count the cells containing a 9. Remember that a 4 on the first die and a 5
      on the second is a different outcome from a 5 on the first die and a 4 on
      the second.
    answer: 0.1111
    tolerance: 0.005
    explanation: >
      There are four ways to make a 9 — (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), and (6,3) — out of
      36 equally likely outcomes, so P(9) = 4 / 36 = .11.
  - id: sums_eleven_outcomes
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      There are 11 possible sums (2 through 12) but 36 outcomes in the sample
      space. How many outcomes produce a sum of 7?
    answer: 6
    tolerance: 0
    explanation: >
      Six: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), and (6,1). The 11 sums are not
      equally likely precisely because different numbers of outcomes produce
      them, which is why we count outcomes rather than sums.
  - id: corner_three_eight_ten
    type: numeric
    prompt: >
      Over on the right of the board, one corner touches tiles numbered 3, 8,
      and 10. What is the probability that it produces something on a given
      roll — that is, the probability of rolling a 3, an 8, or a 10?
    hint: >
      A single roll cannot be two different sums at once, so no outcome gets
      counted twice. Add up the ways.
    answer: 0.2778
    tolerance: 0.005
    explanation: >
      There are two ways to roll a 3, five ways to roll an 8, and three ways to
      roll a 10, and no outcome is more than one of them, so
      P(3 or 8 or 10) = (2 + 5 + 3) / 36 = 10 / 36 = .28.
```
